messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Detected surge in OOMs for paged-attention allocator in us-west1-gpu (last 10m). 42 OOMs, 16 pod restarts. Suspected KV cache fragmentation + slow memory creep. Metrics: alloc_fail_rate↑, pager_evictions↑. Dashboard: https://ops.internal/r/alerts/3925001234

Maya K: grabbing first touch. Which services and customers are seeing errors?

Raj P: small-prod and two midmarket customers reporting 502/503s and elevated tail latencies (99p -> ~8s). Pods show exit code 137 and CUDA OOMs in kubelet logs.

Elena S: quick note from host: nvml logs show repeated GPU OOMs on GPU0, kernel shows GPU reset. Runtime logs showing repeated allocation retries + fragmentation warnings: "requested contiguous pages=256MB, largest_free=32MB".

Tom W: sounds like contiguous slab starvation from paged allocator fragmentation. Slow leak + fragmentation gives gradual inability to satisfy larger contiguous allocations (attention KV pages).

Lin H: runbook steps I'm thinking: 1) Identify hot pods: `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime -o wide` 2) For affected pods, `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` node(s) if node-level? 3) Patch configmap to increase eviction aggressiveness (temporary) or lower model batch sizes. 4) Canary rolling restart.

Maya K: running pod list now:
```
$ kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime -o wide
NAME                           READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE   NODE
runtime-5f7c8d7c9b-2k9lz      0/2     CrashLoop 5          12m   us-west1-gpu-a-03
runtime-5f7c8d7c9b-hx4pz      1/2     Running   0          3h    us-west1-gpu-b-01
runtime-7d9f3d4e2c-ptm6r      0/2     CrashLoop 3          8m    us-west1-gpu-a-02
```

Maya K: tail from one of crashlooping pods:
```
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] runtime: allocation failed: cudaErrorMemoryAllocation: out of memory
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] allocator: paged_attn: couldn't find contiguous chunk of 128MB, largest_free=24MB
[2026-03-15T02:10:12Z] process exiting with code 137
```

Raj P: confirmed exit 137 + `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation`. Also seeing `GC: attempted evict but KV cache pinned pages prevented reclaim`. Looks like pinned pages + fragmentation -> slow creep to OOM.

Elena S: immediate mitigations we can do now: - Reduce per-request max_seq for heavy models (env override) - Toggle `PAGED_ATTN_EVICT_THRESHOLD` to 0.55 from 0.8 for canary - Roll canary to 2 pods behind LB - If node-level, `kubectl cordon` + `kubectl drain` the worst offenders to force cold starts (which free fragmented memory temporally).

Tom W: agree. Also consider temporarily disabling attention paging for models > 16k tokens (config flag) until we have a more robust defrag.

Maya K: applying canary config change to `runtime-config` configmap now (patch):
```
kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data": {"PAGED_ATTN_EVICT_THRESHOLD":"0.55"}}'
kubectl -n inference rollout restart deploy/runtime --field-selector metadata.name=runtime --selector env=canary
```

ops-bot: Created incident ticket INC-2026-1438 and paged the on-call SRE rotation. Slack incident channel: #inc-3925001234. Pager call: @pager.

Lin H: monitoring note: watch `paged_attn_fragmentation_ratio` and `kv_cache_pinned_pages`. If fragmentation_ratio > 0.7 we should escalate to infra for node kernel parameter changes (largepage/defrag tweaks).

Maya K: canary pods restarted, two canary pods stable for 3m, no OOMs so far. Rolling restart of next 10% slicing now.

Raj P: early telemetry looks promising: OOM count down from 42->6 in last 8m on canary nodes. Tail lat 99p trending back to baseline. Customer impact: currently ~25 customers had transient 5-30s errors; no persisted data loss. We're proactively emailing affected customers.

Elena S: note for follow-up: capture heap / nvml snapshots from affected nodes. Run `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.used,memory.free --format=csv` and collect `dmesg` + runtime heap profile.

Tom W: scheduling a short node maintenance window to roll the three worst nodes and apply `vm.zone_reclaim_mode` and `transparent_hugepage=never` changes we discussed in infra backlog. This should reduce fragmentation pressure. ETA 35m.

Maya K: handoff to night SRE in 20m. Current state for handoff message: mitigation in place (evict threshold lowered + canary rollout), OOMs reduced but not fully eliminated; rolling node maintenance planned; customer impact: 25 customers transient 5-30s errors, status page updated.

Elena S: leaving runbook snippet for the next oncall: 
- check `kubectl -n inference get pods -l app=runtime`
- inspect `runtime` logs for `allocator: paged_attn` and `cudaErrorMemoryAllocation`
- set `PAGED_ATTN_EVICT_THRESHOLD=0.55` in configmap for canary
- restart canary pods, wait 5m, then gradual rollout 10% -> 25% -> 50%
- if OOM persists, cordon+drain worst nodes and escalate to infra for kernel param change
- collect nvml/dmesg/heap snapshots and attach to INC ticket

Maya K: handoff: tagging @Lin_H for infra follow-up, @Elena_S for postmortem, @Raj_P for customer comms. Leaving shift now. All logs and commands in incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

Elena S: thanks team. Will monitor for another hour, then we open postmortem once steady. Key action items for postmortem: root cause analysis of KV cache pinning, improve eviction heuristics, add automated defrag or background compaction, and add alert that correlates fragmentation ratio + pinned pages (to reduce noise).

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-1438 updated: status=mitigating, severity=high, impact=partial, customers_affected=~25, next_update=+30m.

Raj P: leaving final note — observed one CUDA driver reset in the last 10m, probably from OOM. If we see driver resets persist after node maintenance, escalate to GPU vendor support.

Elena S: handing off to night SRE @Maya_K (oncall) for watch. Handoff summary saved to INC-2026-1438.

Maya K: out — thanks all, good triage, see y'all in postmortem. :v:
